title: Cash that became an IOU from a related company
question: In which years did a nursing home's cash fall by millions while the amount its owners' other companies owed it rose by about as much?
finding: 11 Bay Area home-years since 2013 (45 in California) show cash and securities falling by $5 million or more and the net amount owed by related parties rising by at least three quarters of the fall: $200.8 million in all. 8 are in 2025, moving $173.3 million: Cedar Crest Nursing and Rehabilitation Center (cash $36.0 million to $0, owed by related parties $7.3 million to $45.6 million); Plum Tree Care Center (cash $35.2 million to $0, owed by related parties $6.5 million to $43.2 million); Vista Manor Nursing Center (cash $34.9 million to $0, owed by related parties $3.7 million to $41.0 million); Pleasanton Nursing and Rehabilitation Center (cash $31.5 million to $478,409, owed by related parties $15.4 million to $49.3 million); Smith Ranch Skilled Nursing & Rehabilitation Ctr (cash $13.2 million to $398,321, owed by related parties -$13.1 million to $605,414); Lawton Skilled Nursing & Rehabilitation Center (cash $9.1 million to $218,549, owed by related parties -$11.2 million to -$2.7 million).
how: Cash and securities are the State pivot profiles' "Cash & Securities" figure (pivot profiles 2012-2018 and 2023-2025, trend pivot for 2019-2022), at the end of the last report filed in the year. The amount owed by related parties is the case's net figure from the complete data sets (pivot profiles for 2012-2014). A home-year is listed when cash fell by at least $5 million from the year before and the net related-party balance rose by at least 75% of that fall.
limits: Moving a home's cash into the chain's central account is common treasury practice and is permitted; the home still reports the money as its asset. The question is whether the related company can repay it. 2025 reports are as submitted, not audited, and a reclassification between lines (cash held by the parent first shown as cash, later as a receivable) produces the same pattern without any money moving.
